what_happened: On job 20261025-033731-5hac (a prompts job), the user corrected the accepted reading 1. The reading would have listed the banned boundary words in the file, which makes the boundary scan fail on that file. The user changed it to point to boundary_words() in xtask/tests/policy.rs without listing the words. The user also added facts the reading lacked, each to be given with its source. An SSH remote like git@host:owner/repo looks like an email and admission refuses it. GitHub caches are scoped per pull request and per branch, and only main writes main's shared caches. The reader prompt set has 3 tokens of room (1997 of 2000) and the change verifier has 2 (1298 of 1300). Producers, planner, critic and reader cannot see records/. The early pull request opens before Athena's checks, and land waits for its CI run before pushing the landing commit.
cause: The reader is given the request but no list of the constraints that earlier incidents exposed. Those are the boundary-word scan, the email-literal admission rule, CI cache scoping, per-set token room, what each role can see, and the PR and land ordering. They exist as separate classes of past failure and as test code. Nothing feeds them into the reading or checks the reading against them. A reading that writes text into Athena's own files therefore looks complete, and only the user, who remembers the incidents, can fill the gaps. The token room is also not reported per prompt set, so budget problems repeat.
prevention: Keep one committed, machine-readable list of the known constraints on text written into Athena's files. Each entry would have a short statement, a source pointer and, where possible, a check. Give it to the reader and planner for any request that writes prompt or doc content. Add a code check that scans a reading's proposed content before dispatch. It would reject listed boundary words, email-like strings such as SSH remotes, and any addition larger than a prompt set's remaining token room. The check should print the remaining room per set.
proposed_request: Create a single constraints reference for writers of Athena prompts and docs, and make the reader and planner use it. Outcome: (1) a committed file that states each known constraint with its source, without listing banned words and pointing to boundary_words() in xtask/tests/policy.rs instead. It covers: SSH remotes like [email]:owner/repo read as email addresses and are refused at admission (use https URLs; allow-list in athena.toml [personal_data]); GitHub caches are scoped per pull request (refs/pull/N/merge) and per branch, and main's shared caches are written only from main; the reader set is at 1997 of 2000 tokens and the change verifier at 1298 of 1300; producers, planner, critic and reader cannot see records/; the early pull request opens before Athena's checks and land waits for its CI run before pushing the landing commit. (2) The reader and planner are told to consult it when a request adds prompt or doc text. (3) A code check reports each prompt set's remaining token room and rejects a reading whose added text exceeds it. Do not make line wrapping or other formatting a blocking criterion. While editing, run only the scoped tests for the crates touched, and run the full suite at most once at the end.
